title: Morning Intel
bullets: Markets: Wall Street closed the Black Friday shortened session (Nov 27) sharply higher — S&P 500 +1.2%, Nasdaq +1.5%, Dow +1% — as a tech/chip rebound (Micron, SanDisk +10%) capped a winning week.
Markets: All three major indexes finished November higher overall, clawing back a volatile month marked by an AI-stock selloff mid-month.
Companies: Nvidia stays in flux — the board rejected Jensen Huang's bid to return as CEO despite a record $116B quarterly revenue beat; CFO Colette Kress continues as interim chief.
Companies: Palo Alto Networks (PANW), HP (HPQ) and SPCX drew attention in earnings/news flow as trading resumed post-Thanksgiving.

Macro/Policy: The Fed, now under Chair Kevin Warsh, held rates steady at 3.5%-3.75% in October; about half of officials project a hike by year-end, a hawkish shift markets are weighing ahead of the December meeting.
Macro/Policy: Black Friday online spending is forecast to hit a record (~$12.9B, +9.2% YoY per Adobe); final Mastercard/Adobe tallies for 2026 were not yet available at publish time.
